nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to target BP <130/80 mmHg or max 10 mg daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin blockade to slow CKD progression and reduce proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine & potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and if eGFR falls <20 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.purpose: Reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular risk in patients with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends dapagliflozin 10 mg for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² (TA775)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and uptitrate to 40 mg if LDL >1.8 mmol/L after 4‑6 weeks
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a risk‑equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203: all CKD patients should receive a statin (e.g., atorvastatin 20 mg)

medications.dose: 1 g orally every 6‑8 hours PRN (max 4 g/24 h)
medications.purpose: Replace chronic NSAID (naproxen) to avoid nephrotoxicity
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises avoidance of chronic NSAIDs in CKD; paracetamol is safe

medications.dose: Continue current regimen; consider 10‑20% dose reduction after starting dapagliflozin
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for type 2 and CF‑related diabetes
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management guideline (NICE NG28) – required for glucose control; not a CKD‑specific drug

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive risk of acute kidney injury, hyperkalaemia and reduced antihypertensive effect
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue naproxen; monitor renal function and potassium after starting ramipril

interactions_checked.interaction: Synergistic glucose‑lowering effect increasing hypoglycaemia risk
interactions_checked.action: Reduce prandial insulin dose by 10‑20% and monitor capillary glucose closely for 2 weeks

contraindications.reason: Chronic NSAIDs accelerate CKD progression and increase risk of AKI in eGFR 30.5 mL/min/1.73 m² (NG203 contraindicated drugs)

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure not provided – assume not at target; will titrate ramipril to <130/80 mmHg.
Serum potassium and liver function tests not available – order baseline labs before initiating ramipril and atorvastatin.
Urine ACR value not recorded – obtain spot ACR for baseline proteinuria monitoring.
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin or sulfonamides unknown – verify before prescribing.
HbA1c not provided – obtain to guide insulin dose adjustment when adding dapagliflozin.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril, dapagliflozin and atorvastatin as first‑line CKD therapies per NICE NG203, replace chronic naproxen with paracetamol, and continue insulin with dose reduction after SGLT2‑i initiation. Monitor BP, renal function, potassium, liver enzymes, ACR and glucose; review medications annually.
